text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--The government plans to sell all or part of its 52 percent stake in Tele Danmark, currently worth over 23 billion crowns at market prices.
--The far left Socialist People's Party is still unconvinced that the new Amsterdam treaty enshrines unequivocally the Danish EU optouts, particulalry in the area of border controls.

--All indications are that Aarhus Flydedok will take over bankrupt Svendborg Shipyard, saving it. Under the plan Aarhus Flydedok would buy all of Svendborg and lease the new construction section to Morsoe Shipyard.

--Family house prices are on average 50 percent higher than four years ago and rising property prices are spurring new construction, bringing the risk of wage inflation in the building industry. To reduce this risk the government should cut public building projects.

--Electronics firm Chartec will go public this year. It is expected to quadruple turnover to 100 million crowns in 1998 and its exchange listing will bring it the necessary capital for expansion. REUTER
